title: Band personalities, dice on the bus and card games
summary: Sweets was funny, and Lester Young and Vic Dickenson rolled dice on the bus and were first to go broke. She loaned them money, played tonk and poker, and won against men who thought she did not know how.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: I mean, you were born and brought up in the South but, I mean, you hadn't had to go from place to place.
No.
That must have been pretty hard. And then, I mean, there were all the different personalities in the Band.
Yeah, but they were all so nice. Just the nicest bunch. I don't know, of course, Sweets, he was something else.
A funny guy you mean?

Yeah, he was really funny. And Lester and Vic Dickenson, they used to just keep us going all the time. Because we'd be on the bus and we'd be sleeping and we'd hear the dice clicking. They'd say, 'wake up, come on here and let's get this stuff on the road here'. They'd say, 'this is our lucky day', and they'd be the first ones broke.
Oh, that's funny.

How did everybody do it? Did you get out in the isle?
Yeah.
And how many people would get in on the game?
Well, whoever wanted to shoot.
There wouldn't be a lot of room.
No.
Who were they lucky guys? Were there any lucky guys?
Well, some of them were and some of them wasn't.
Would Basie be in on the game?
Yeah, he'd play too. Everybody would play.
It passes the time, doesn't it?
Yeah.

Yeah.
But would they keep on drawing money in advance to keep on going?
Oh yeah, you had to do that I guess because they just like to play cards all the time. They would get into places where they would play poker. Sometimes we'd play tonk.
